messages:
alex_m: Heads-up: after last kernel chooser change I'm seeing spikes in mem fragmentation -> sporadic OOMs in 2x batch runs.
priya: can you paste the profile? rough numbers help.
alex_m: profiler snippet:
```
Batch=2, Seq=2048, Model=redwood-7b, GPU=A100-40GB
Allocated peak: 38.6GB
Free fragments: 1.2GB in 3 slabs
OOM at commit: allocate workspace 512MB failed
Kernel picked: FlashAttentionV2 (requires workspace ~1.1GB) -> fell back to Triton
``` 
marc: interesting — kernel chooser picked FA2 but fallback path to Triton still tried to reserve FA workspace first?
steph: we keep a conservative allocation path: chooser probes ideal kernel and reserves worst-case ws, then tries smaller kernels. That reservation can fragment.
alex_m: right. with kv-cache warm and prefix lengths ~512, the mem pressure is much higher.
priya: proposal: move to slab allocator for transient kernel workspaces with size buckets (64MB,128MB,256MB,512MB,1GB) and don't allocate worst-case until kernel actually launches. lazy-reserve.
marc: bucketized slabs + LRU free-list for transient buffers sounds good. Two caveats: (1) alignment for cuBLASLt (need 256B) (2) FlashAttention sometimes needs contiguous cfg memory >1GB.
steph: for (1) we can ensure slab alignment by rounding to 256B. for (2) we can fallback to a dedicated large-slab pool per-device for contiguous >512MB requests.
alex_m: also want low-overhead path for common small workspaces (<=128MB) to reduce fragmentation.
priya: additionally, add heuristics: if kv-cache occupancy > 60% of its reserved quota, reduce kernel workspace reservations by 25% (best-effort) and prefer cuBLASLt kernels which use smaller ws but slightly higher compute.
marc: sounds risky for perf. we need A/B: small perf tests with 1k samples. If quality OK, then enable adaptive reduction as opt-in.
steph: I'll add an env flag: RUNTIME_WS_STRATEGY=slab_lazy_v1 and a toggle for adaptive_kv_pressure.
alex_m: for repro, here's a lightweight repro script to trigger the path:
```
# run 2 parallel chats to warm kv
python bench.py --model redwood-7b --seq 2048 --batch 2 --prefix-warm 512 --iters 10
```
marc: can you share before/after traces? look for allocations pattern: alloc/free count, largest_free_chunk.
alex_m: attached the flame trace (pseudolog):
```
alloc 512MB workspace -> split slab 256+256
free 256MB -> leaves 256MB fragment
alloc 1.1GB -> fail (no contiguous)
fallback to Triton -> alloc 640MB -> works
result: extra fragmentation -> next run OOM
```
priya: good. next steps: steph to prototype slab allocator + lazy-reserve, infra to run perf job comparing latency/throughput on 500 samples, marc to craft safety canary (auto-disable slab on >1% error/regression), alex to collect additional repro traces.
steph: will PR today with tests, but need decision on default: opt-in for now.
alex_m: thanks. if we can avoid reserving worst-case flash ws until commit, we should reduce runtime OOMs a lot.
marc: add a guard: if preferred kernel gives >10% latency improvement, keep explicit reserve; else lazy.
priya: agree. let's sync after perf run. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: scheduled perf job #987 on pool-a100. ETA 45m.
